findings.premise: Current QueueAdmission sanitizes host callback failures separately from module validation and persistence failures.
findings.evidence: Read append(), bind(), sameEnvelope() and policyFailure(), plus FileQueue.persist(). The callback alone is wrapped by `try { output = await this.#policy.admit(...) } catch ...`; snapshotting, sameEnvelope and persist run afterward. policyFailure preserves only UNBOUND_PROJECT/POLICY_DENIED and otherwise returns NOT_READY. The proposed transform placement accurately preserves this boundary. findings.action: Implement the hooks at the specified boundaries and retain separate callback-origin versus module-origin error tests.

findings.premise: The existing runtime supports ordered multiple OwnedWork participants and retains ownership when quiescence or release fails.
findings.evidence: Read the complete runtime lifecycle and its tests. stopAdmission visits every participant; quiesce drains serially then waits for models; after successful quiescence close attempts every participant release in array order and releases the owner only when all succeed. The existing three-participant failure test asserts ordered closes and retained ownership. Drain rejection intentionally prevents entry into resource release. findings.action: Add the planned real queue/store two-participant tests; preserve the existing requirement that release follows verified quiescence.

findings.premise: The authoritative store is new, while S1 ownership and S2 receipt verification are reusable with the stated roles.
findings.evidence: Package source inspection found no MemoryStore/CommitPlan implementation; host-node currently constructs only FileQueue and QueueAdmission. findings.premise: Receipt retention and replay matching remain compatible with S2 after acknowledgment, recycling and logical forgetting.

findings.premise: The proposed admission and queue/store ordering make validation failures and uncertain outcomes detectable without silently repeating effects.
findings.evidence: Current queue persistence, proof matching and acknowledgment support the proposed reconciliation order. The LLD specifies module validation outside host sanitization, reservation release on pre-persist failure, immutable historical conflicts, store fencing on uncertainty, proof availability during queue close, partial-open rollback and owner retention when settlement is unverified. It prohibits store-to-queue callbacks and places ACK after lane release. findings.premise: The pinned native SDK path can satisfy the required crash-durable atomic publication contract on both supported platforms.
findings.evidence: Inspected lance-probe.mjs and qualification-probe.json. They establish a one-version merge, nullable vectors, pinned reads and normal-exit reopen on Darwin Node 22.23.2, but explicitly exclude crash/fsync and Linux qualification. The official [Table API](https://lancedb.github.io/lancedb/js/classes/Table/) and [merge API](https://lancedb.github.io/lancedb/js/classes/MergeInsertBuilder/) describe the operations, not this exact platform durability proof. No S3 crash qualification results were available; the design correctly leaves this as a mandatory gate.
